title: Periscopes & Kaleidoscopes
description: Build the tools of a true light-master. A periscope to spy over Umbra's wall, and a kaleidoscope whose beauty weakens the Shadow Fog.

content.value: A periscope uses two plane mirrors fixed parallel at each end of a tube, each tilted at 45°. Light from the top reflects down the tube and into your eye, letting you see over walls or above water. Submarines use periscopes to look above the sea while staying hidden below.

top mirror  🪞 (45°)  ◀── light from above
       │
       ▼   light travels down the tube
       │
 bottom mirror 🪞 (45°) ──▶ 👁️ your eye

A kaleidoscope uses two or three mirror strips joined to form a tube. Loose coloured beads at one end are reflected many times by the mirrors. Because the mirrors sit at a small angle, you see beautiful, symmetrical, repeating patterns — and every twist makes a brand-new one that will never be exactly repeated.
A periscope relies on multiple reflection to bend your view; a kaleidoscope relies on multiple images to multiply patterns. Same physics — different magic!
Key Takeaway: A periscope uses two 45° parallel mirrors to see over obstacles; a kaleidoscope uses angled mirrors to create endless repeating patterns from a few coloured pieces.

quiz.question: A periscope works using…
options: two plane mirrors tilted at 45° at each end of a tube
quiz.explain: Two parallel plane mirrors at 45° reflect light down the tube, letting you see over a wall or above water.

quiz.question: The beautiful repeating patterns in a kaleidoscope are caused by…
options: multiple images formed by angled mirrors
quiz.explain: Angled mirror strips form many reflected images of the coloured beads, creating symmetrical repeating patterns.

quiz.question: Why is a periscope useful for a submarine?
options: It lets the crew see above the water while staying hidden below
quiz.explain: The periscope carries the view from above the surface down to the submerged crew using two reflections.
